successors.text: the Aksumite heartland, Tigray and the Eritrean highlands: 'around 960, a queen known as Gudit (also Yodit or Ésato) conquered Aksum'

ledger.x: c. 50 BC: Aksum rises in Tigray. 'the kingdom was founded in the 1st century' and the polity 'arose between 150 BCE and 150 CE'; the Periplus, 'a trading guide which likely dates to the mid-first century AD', places Aksum within Zoskales's realm. Cliopatria's -50 is inside the page's range but earlier than its…

c. 200: Aksum crosses to Arabia. Gedara 'was the first king to be involved in South Arabian affairs'; his reign gave 'control of much of western Yemen until a joint Himyarite-Sabean alliance pushed them out'. The year is the start of Gedara's reign as the page dates it; the land was Himyarite and Sabaean (Cliopatria's…

c. 275: the Aksumites leave Arabia. 'Sabaean pressure eventually pushed Aksumite forces back' in the late 3rd century; the Monumentum Adulitanum (c. 240-260) is the last record of the campaigns. The year is the researcher's for 'late 3rd century'; Cliopatria keeps the Arabian part to 352.
331: the Aksumite presence at Meroë ends ('for a short period of time'; one year is the researcher's).
525-570: Yemen as an Aksumite tributary (vassal tint, rule 4).

c. 700: the Beja take the northern plateau. The page gives 'the end of the seventh century' and no boundary; the region (Northern Red Sea, Anseba and Gash-Barka) is the researcher's reading. The Beja need a dossier.
c. 800: the capital moves south to Kubar (infobox 'Kubar (after c. 800)'); the site is unknown, so the map's dot stays at Aksum. Cliopatria's keyframe at 806 may mark this.

c. 960: Gudit conquers Aksum. The kingdom 'collapsed under uncertain circumstances around 960'; 'around 960, a queen known as Gudit (also Yodit or Ésato) conquered Aksum'; the last ruler Dil Na'od '917 or 940-960'. The Zagwe 'succeeded Aksum in the eleventh or twelfth century (most likely…

wars.name: Aksumite intervention in South Arabia
wars.outcome: Gedara (c. 200-230) took 'much of western Yemen until a joint Himyarite-Sabean alliance pushed them out'; late in the 3rd century 'Sabaean pressure eventually pushed Aksumite forces back'. Drawn as an occupation.

wars.name: Aksumite campaign against Meroë
wars.outcome: 'conquering Meroë under Ezana in 330 for a short period of time'; the Meroë page dates the destruction to 350 and the Kush page an Atbara expedition after 340; the Ezana page calls the evidence inconclusive.

wars.name: Aksumite invasion of Himyar
wars.outcome: Kaleb 'eventually routed Yusuf's forces' (Dhu Nuwas) and installed Sumyafa Ashwa as viceroy; infobox 'Aksumite invasion of Himyar: 518-525'; 'Aksum held on to Southern Arabia from 520 until 525'.

wars.name: Aksumite-Persian wars
wars.outcome: Sasanian victory (infobox 'Establishment of Sasanian Yemen'): Wahrez's 800 Dailamites won at Hadhramaut and took Sana'a in 570, killing Masruq ibn Abraha; after Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan's murder a second expedition of 4,000 'reconquered Yemen by 578'; 'Yemen was…

wars.name: Gudit's conquest of Aksum
wars.outcome: 'around 960, a queen known as Gudit (also Yodit or Ésato) conquered Aksum'; the kingdom collapsed and Gudit's line 'ruled for about 40 years' (Zagwe page) before the Zagwe.
